name: Calcium (Ca)
summary: The most abundant mineral in the body; structural in bone and teeth and essential for muscle contraction, nerve conduction, clotting and enzyme function.

conditions.label: Deficiency (hypocalcaemia / dietary)
conditions.description: Low calcium availability impairs bone mineralisation and raises neuromuscular excitability.

affects.effect: Reduced bone density; osteoporosis and fracture risk
affects.detail: Sustained low intake draws calcium from bone, lowering bone mineral density and increasing fracture risk.

ageModifiers.child: Inadequate calcium plus vitamin D contributes to rickets and poor peak bone mass.
ageModifiers.elderly: Accelerates age-related bone loss and fracture risk.

genderModifiers.female: Post-menopausal oestrogen loss accelerates calcium loss from bone, raising osteoporosis risk.

affects.detail: Low ionised calcium increases neuromuscular excitability, causing cramps, carpopedal spasm and tetany (Chvostek/Trousseau signs).
Severe hypocalcaemia prolongs the cardiac QT interval and can cause arrhythmia.
